acme.proxyUsageNote:
Prerequisite: the domain (or a parent covering subdomains) must be configured in ACME Domains with a DNS provider. The proxy only supports dns-01.

Each external CA account can expose a dedicated endpoint: /acme/proxy/<slug>/directory (enable Expose via ACME proxy in Certificate Authorities (CA)). The default path /acme/proxy/directory follows the account selected in proxy settings.

UCM automatically creates and removes TXT records via that provider. The --manual-auth-hook and --manual-cleanup-hook flags can stay as no-ops (/bin/true) because the proxy performs DNS validation.

Avoid two concurrent requests for the same name (Certbot + UCM UI): the second TXT record can overwrite the first. If the UCM HTTPS certificate is self-signed (lab), add --no-verify-ssl to Certbot.

dnsUpdate.noteCertbot: certbot accepts an IP address as server, not a host name. The default algorithm is HMAC-MD5, which UCM refuses, so always set the algorithm.
dnsUpdate.noteLego: The default algorithm of lego is hmac-sha1, which UCM refuses, so always set the algorithm. Use --dns.propagation-wait when lego cannot see the public zone.
dnsUpdate.noteCertManagerSha384: cert-manager cannot use hmac-sha384. Create a new key with hmac-sha256 or hmac-sha512.

dnsUpdate.noteWinAcmePort: win-acme always sends the update to port 53 (its --serverport is used as a timeout). Make UCM reachable on port 53 with a port mapping.

settings.smtpOauthSetup_google_title: How to get a Gmail Client ID & Secret
settings.smtpOauthSetup_google_steps:
1. Open Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials.
2. Create a new project (or pick one) and enable the 'Gmail API'.
3. Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (type: Web application).
4. Add the redirect URI shown below to the 'Authorized redirect URIs' list.
5. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the fields below.
6. Add your sender email as a 'Test user' on the OAuth consent screen.
settings.smtpOauthSetup_microsoft_steps:
Mobile mail apps (iOS Mail, Thunderbird, etc.) use Microsoft-published client IDs they cannot share. Because UCM is self-hosted, you create your own: it's free and takes 5 minutes:

1. Sign in at the Azure Portal with any Microsoft account (free, no subscription needed).
2. App registrations → New registration → choose 'Personal Microsoft accounts only'.
3. Add the redirect URI shown below (Web platform).
4. Certificates & secrets → New client secret → copy the Value.
5. API permissions → add 'SMTP.Send' and 'offline_access' (Microsoft Graph, delegated).
6. Copy the Application (client) ID and the secret Value into the fields below.
settings.smtpOauthSetup_microsoft365_title: How to set up Microsoft 365 (work / school)
settings.smtpOauthSetup_microsoft365_steps:
1. Sign in at the Azure Portal as a tenant admin.
2. App registrations → New registration → choose 'Accounts in this organizational directory only' (or multitenant).
3. Add the redirect URI shown below (Web platform).
4. Certificates & secrets → New client secret → copy the Value.
5. API permissions → add 'SMTP.Send' and 'offline_access' (Microsoft Graph, delegated) → Grant admin consent.
6. Copy the Application (client) ID, the secret Value, and your Tenant ID (Directory ID) into the fields below.

users_password_scrypt.title: Local users with an scrypt password hash: they cannot sign in once FIPS mode is on
users_password_scrypt.remedy: Have each user sign in once before the switch: the hash is replaced by PBKDF2 automatically; otherwise an administrator resets the password.

users_backup_codes_scrypt.title: Users whose 2FA backup codes are scrypt hashes: those codes stop working in FIPS mode
users_backup_codes_scrypt.remedy: Ask these users to regenerate their backup codes before the switch.

protocols_secret_scrypt.title: EST, WSTEP or XCEP passwords stored as scrypt hashes: clients are refused in FIPS mode
protocols_secret_scrypt.remedy: Enter the password again in the protocol settings: it is then stored as a PBKDF2 hash.

ca_eddsa_key.title: Certificate authorities with an Ed25519 or Ed448 key: they cannot sign in FIPS mode on an HSM, or on a module that does not approve EdDSA
ca_eddsa_key.remedy: Create an RSA or ECDSA (P-256/P-384/P-521) authority and move issuance to it before the switch; an authority key cannot be converted.

ca_weak_key.title: Certificate authorities with a DSA key, RSA of an odd length or outside 2048 to 16384 bits or a curve other than P-256/384/521
ca_weak_key.remedy: Create an authority with RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 and move issuance to it.

ca_unapproved_algorithm.title: Certificate authorities with an ML-DSA key: they cannot sign in FIPS mode on an HSM, or on a module that does not approve ML-DSA
ca_unapproved_algorithm.remedy: Create an RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 authority and move issuance to it before the switch, or keep FIPS mode off while ML-DSA issuance is needed.

ssh_ca_eddsa_key.title: SSH certificate authorities with an Ed25519 key: they cannot sign in FIPS mode on a module that does not approve EdDSA
ssh_ca_eddsa_key.remedy: Create an ECDSA or RSA SSH authority and distribute its public key to the hosts before the switch.

ssh_certificates_eddsa_key.title: Active SSH certificates for Ed25519 keys: they stay valid but cannot be signed again
ssh_certificates_eddsa_key.remedy: Have their holders switch to an ECDSA or RSA key at the next renewal.

deploy_ssh_eddsa_key.title: Deployment targets that sign in with an Ed25519 SSH key: deployments fail in FIPS mode
deploy_ssh_eddsa_key.remedy: Give each target a new ECDSA or RSA key and install its public key on the host.

deploy_ssh_eddsa_host_key.title: Deployment targets pinned to an Ed25519 host key: deployments fail in FIPS mode until the pin is reset
deploy_ssh_eddsa_host_key.remedy: Make sure each host also has an ECDSA or RSA host key, then reset the pinned host key of the target: the next connection pins that key.

ocsp_responder_unapproved_key.title: Delegated OCSP responders with an Ed25519/Ed448, ML-DSA or weak key: the CA signs instead
ocsp_responder_unapproved_key.remedy: Issue a new RSA or ECDSA responder certificate and select it in the CA settings.

tsa_signer_unapproved_key.title: The timestamping certificate has an Ed25519/Ed448, ML-DSA or weak key: timestamps fail in FIPS mode
tsa_signer_unapproved_key.remedy: Issue a new RSA or ECDSA timestamping certificate and select it in the TSA settings.

certificates_unapproved_key.title: Active certificates with an Ed25519/Ed448 or ML-DSA key, RSA of an odd length or outside 2048 to 16384 bits or another curve
certificates_unapproved_key.remedy: They stay valid; renew them with a new RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 key, since renewing with the same key is refused in FIPS mode.

templates_unapproved_key_type.title: Active templates whose key type is not FIPS approved: issuance from them is refused
templates_unapproved_key_type.remedy: Change the key type of these templates to RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521.

policies_unapproved_key_type.title: Active policies that allow key types FIPS mode removes (Ed25519, Ed448, ML-DSA, short RSA...)
policies_unapproved_key_type.remedy: Remove those key types from the policies; a policy left with none allows no issuance.

acme_client_unapproved_key_type.title: ACME client settings or renewing orders that use a key type FIPS mode refuses
acme_client_unapproved_key_type.remedy: Set the ACME client key type to RSA or ECDSA and re-create these orders with a new key.

hsm_softhsm.title: SoftHSM providers: SoftHSM is not a validated module, keys on it are not FIPS protected
hsm_softhsm.remedy: Move the keys to a validated HSM, or accept SoftHSM as a test setup only.

hsm_gcp_grpc.title: Google Cloud KMS providers: their client uses gRPC with its own TLS, outside the FIPS module
hsm_gcp_grpc.remedy: Prefer a PKCS#11, Azure Key Vault or OpenBao provider for keys that must stay in FIPS scope.

hsm_unapproved_keys.title: HSM keys FIPS mode refuses (RSA of an odd length or outside 2048 to 16384 bits, curves other than P-256/P-384/P-521, Ed25519, Ed448, ML-DSA, ChaCha20-Poly1305, unknown types)
hsm_unapproved_keys.remedy: Replace them with RSA 2048+, ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 or AES keys; in FIPS mode, OpenBao and Vault Transit keys of these types are no longer listed.

dns_tsig_hmac_md5.title: RFC 2136 DNS providers signing with TSIG hmac-md5: DNS-01 updates are refused in FIPS mode
dns_tsig_hmac_md5.remedy: Create an hmac-sha256 TSIG key on the DNS server and enter it in the provider.

session_short_secret_key.title: The session key (SECRET_KEY) is under 14 bytes: in FIPS mode no CSRF token can be issued or checked with it, so every sign-in fails
session_short_secret_key.remedy: Set a SECRET_KEY of 32 characters or more in the service environment and restart.

hmac_short_secret.title: HMAC secrets under 14 bytes (webhook secrets, RFC 2136 TSIG keys, Constellix, DNS Made Easy, INWX and Tencent Cloud secrets, external EAB keys of ACME accounts): the FIPS module does not approve them; FIPS mode refuses to save a webhook secret or TSIG key this short, and every one of them but a TSIG key fails when used
hmac_short_secret.remedy: Regenerate the webhook secrets and create TSIG keys of at least 14 bytes (hmac-sha256 keys of 32 bytes are the usual size), ask the DNS provider or the ACME CA for a secret or EAB key of 14 bytes or more, then update the receivers, DNS servers, providers and accounts.

msca_winrm_ntlm.title: Microsoft CA connections whose WinRM channel uses NTLM: the channel is refused in FIPS mode
msca_winrm_ntlm.remedy: Turn off the WinRM channel of these connections. Kerberos replaces NTLM only on a native install whose Kerberos library is built on the system OpenSSL (RHEL); the Kerberos library of the Docker image does its own cryptography, so FIPS mode refuses Kerberos there too.

msca_kerberos_outside_fips.title: Microsoft CA connections that sign in with Kerberos (certsrv or the WinRM channel) on a Kerberos library that does its own cryptography, outside the FIPS module: their sign-in is refused in FIPS mode
msca_kerberos_outside_fips.remedy: Switch these connections to certificate or Basic authentication and turn off their Kerberos WinRM channel, or run UCM from the package on a system whose Kerberos library is built on the system OpenSSL (RHEL); the Kerberos library of the Docker image is not.

kerberos_acceptor_outside_fips.title: Windows enrollment profiles served over Kerberos (XCEP and WSTEP) on a Kerberos library that does its own cryptography, outside the FIPS module: the Kerberos binding answers 503 in FIPS mode
kerberos_acceptor_outside_fips.remedy: Enroll these clients over the UsernamePassword or Certificate binding, or run UCM from the package on a system whose Kerberos library is built on the system OpenSSL (RHEL); the Kerberos library of the Docker image is not.

backup_schedule_argon2id.title: Scheduled backups are written with Argon2id: such archives cannot be restored in FIPS mode
backup_schedule_argon2id.remedy: Set the scheduled backup KDF to PBKDF2, and take a manual backup with kdf "pbkdf2" before the switch.

backup_archives_argon2id.title: Backup archives encrypted with Argon2id: they cannot be restored in FIPS mode
backup_archives_argon2id.remedy: Keep them for a standard instance, and take a manual backup with kdf "pbkdf2" before the switch.

database_postgres_without_tls.title: The PostgreSQL connection runs over TCP without sslmode=require or stricter: UCM refuses to start in FIPS mode
database_postgres_without_tls.remedy: Enable TLS on the server and add sslmode=require (or verify-full) to DATABASE_URL; for a server on the same host, connect through its Unix socket instead: postgresql://ucm:<password>@/ucm?host=/var/run/postgresql

database_postgres_gssenc.title: PostgreSQL is set to use GSSAPI encryption, which runs in the Kerberos library outside the FIPS module: UCM refuses to start in FIPS mode
database_postgres_gssenc.remedy: Remove gssencmode from DATABASE_URL and PGGSSENCMODE from the environment, or set them to disable: TLS then protects the connection.

keys_no_master_key.title: Private keys are stored unencrypted (no master key, or encryption disabled)
keys_no_master_key.remedy: Enable private key encryption in Settings > Security, or provide /etc/ucm/master.key or KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY; with UCM_REQUIRE_KEY_ENCRYPTION=true, UCM then refuses to start without one.

https_unapproved_key.title: The HTTPS certificate has an Ed25519/Ed448, ML-DSA or weak key: the web server cannot use it in FIPS mode
https_unapproved_key.remedy: Install an RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 certificate in the HTTPS settings.

sso.enforce2faHelp: Require users of this provider to enrol a second factor. LDAP sign-ins then ask for it; OIDC and SAML sign-ins rely on the identity provider for MFA.

policies.fipsRulesDesc: FIPS mode applies a system policy ahead of these: RSA keys of an even length from 2048 to 16384 bits, EC P-256 to P-521, and Ed25519, Ed448 and ML-DSA when the loaded FIPS module approves them; SHA-256 to SHA-512 signatures. Policies here can only narrow it.

On the issue form, CSR signing, renewals, approved requests, ACME, SCEP, EST and WSTEP, a request with more DNS names than the maximum is also refused and the validity is capped. The DNS pattern scopes which requests the policy applies to.

msca.title: Microsoft AD CS
msca.subtitle: Manage Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services connections.
msca.helpDescription:
Connect to Microsoft AD CS to sign certificates using your Windows Certificate Authority. Three authentication methods available:

- **Client Certificate (recommended)**: Most secure and standalone. No domain join required. Generate a client cert on your MS CA, export as PFX, then upload the cert and key here.
- **Basic Auth**: Simple username/password over HTTPS. Works without domain join. Ensure the certsrv web enrollment is configured to accept basic authentication in IIS.
- **Kerberos (optional)**: Requires the pyspnego[kerberos] pip package and the machine to be joined to the AD domain (or a keytab configured). Only needed if other auth methods are disabled on the CA.
